name: nhs-ae-four-hour-decline

task.question: For an NHS England provider operating a consultant-led (Type 1) A&E department with at least 100 Type 1 attendances in each of months M and M+1, will the provider's Type 1 within-4-hour performance rate decline in month M+1 relative to month M, given the provider's monthly A&E series (attendances by department type, over-4-hour counts, decision-to-admit waits, emergency admissions) for all months through M, plus the calendar?
task.prediction_time: At the publication of month M's monthly A&E CSV: observed 9, 13 and 10 days after the period end for June, July and August 2026, so the task uses the MAXIMUM observed lag (13 days) rather than a mean - no month's data is used before it existed. Every feature is derived from the provider's monthly series for months <= M, and every eligibility test uses those same months; the label is month M+1's within-4-hour rate versus month M's, published about a month later. The instant is the publication date, not the period end: at the end of month M these values did not yet exist.

prediction_instant.citation: NHS England publishes monthly A&E activity about ten days after the month ends; e.g. August 2026 data was published 2026-09-10

row_selection.basis: eligibility counts the provider's volume-gated months at or before M; the target month M+1 is used only to compute the label, never to decide whether a row exists

timing.observations_note: NHS England published 9, 13 and 10 days after the period end in these three months. The instant uses the MAXIMUM observed lag, not the mean, so no month's data is used before it existed.

feature_documentation: every source field is documented in NHS England's A&E Attendances and Emergency Admissions statistics (column meanings recorded in the candidate record from the publisher's work area; the derived-column dictionary lives in build.py's module docstring and ships in the release DATA_DICTIONARY); month M columns are published before the prediction instant and month M+1 columns are not shipped at all

measurements.unit: proportion of Type 1 attendances within 4 hours (1 - over4/att1)
measurements.frame: month M, the feature month ending at the prediction instant

measurements.unit: count of Type 1 A&E attendances in month M
measurements.frame: month M; >= 100 by the volume gate
stable provider identity; also the clustered-event key

measurements.unit: YYYY-MM of the target month M+1
measurements.frame: the month the label is drawn from; the prediction instant is the end of the previous month
within4h_rate(M+1) < within4h_rate(M), computed from month M+1's source row only

id_columns_note: row_id names one provider-target-month with one label; org codes legitimately repeat across splits because the same providers are tracked over time - the entity is the provider-month, not the provider
positive_events_note: distinct_events counts distinct positive Org Codes per window - the conservative independent-unit count, per the candidate record
